items.title: Carrier group headed to Middle East to replace USS Lincoln, US official says
items.content: Nearly six months into the US-Iran conflict, the Strait of Hormuz remains largely blocked and global oil stockpiles are diminishing. Trump said he plans to declare the strait a US territory after 'we finish defeating Iran.' No genuine endgame in sight.

items.title: Retail Sales Take a Dip, Stocks Eye Weekly Gain
items.content: US retail sales dipped while stocks eyed weekly gains. The Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) fell to new 2026 lows below 14.4 and remains near those today at 14.52, implying little downside hedging. Focus shifts to the Fed's Jackson Hole conference Aug 27-29.

items.title: Stock market news for Aug. 13, 2026: S&P 500 record close
items.content: The S&P 500 rose 0.65% to a closing record of 7,798.99 and surpassed 7,800 intraday for the first time ever; the Dow Jones also posted a fresh record high.

items.title: Hang Seng slips 0.8% to 25,440 on fading US-Iran deal hopes
items.content: The Hang Seng Index slipped 0.8% to close at 25,440 on Wednesday as fading hopes for a US-Iran deal and caution ahead of the latest US inflation data weighed on investor sentiment. Investors also monitored earnings and China tech sector developments.

items.title: Trump insists US controls Hormuz, Iran says it could 'prolong' war with US
items.content: Trump insisted the US still has control over the Strait of Hormuz, threatening Iran would 'get blown away' if it tried to 'do something.' In recent weeks the waterway has once again become center-stage in the conflict.

items.title: China stocks end mixed as semiconductor and AI gains offset US tariff concerns
items.content: The Shanghai Composite was flat at 3,927.2 while the Shenzhen Component rose 0.45% to 14,354.3. Semiconductor stocks gained after SMIC reported a more than threefold increase in second-quarter profit, helped by strong demand for AI-related chips.

items.title: Hong Kong raises economic forecast after best half-yearly performance in 5 years
items.content: Hong Kong raised its full-year 2026 GDP growth forecast to a range of 3.5-4.5% after expansion of 4.3% in Q2, supported by buoyant external trade (June merchandise exports +53.4% y/y) and resilient domestic demand.
